## When the window fills

A model reads a limited number of tokens at once. This limit is the
context window. When a conversation grows past it, each engine fails in
its own way. The exception message usually mentions the context, the KV
cache or `n_ctx`.

Three names refer to the window size. `ctx` is the portable option, in
tokens, that urai passes to the backend. `n_ctx` is the name that
llama.cpp uses, and urai accepts it as an alias of `ctx`.
`chat.ctx_limit` is an attribute that a backend sets to the window size
it uses. [`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat)
does not define it. `chat.pct_full` and the tool loop read `ctx_limit`,
and a value of 0 means that the window size is unknown.

`is_ctx_error(chat, e)` returns `True` when exception `e` from a backend
means that the window is full. It checks two things in order. First it
looks for a known phrase in the lowercased message. Then it checks
whether `chat.pct_full` is at least 1 while `chat.ctx_limit` is set. It
returns `False` when that check raises an error. The tool loop uses it
to decide when to try recovery. The tool loop raises
[`ContextWindowExceededError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#contextwindowexceedederror)
when recovery also fails.

The tool loop writes three message strings into the history.

</tr>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>budget_msg_</code></td>
<td>The tool-call budget (<code>max_steps</code>) runs out</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cancel_msg_</code></td>
<td>The user stops a turn before a tool call runs</td>
</tr>
<tr>

### ContextWindowExceededError

``` python
def ContextWindowExceededError(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*Raised when the context window filled and recovering from it also
failed.*

``` python
class _Fake: ctx_limit, pct_full = 0, 0
test_eq(is_ctx_error(_Fake(), ValueError('n_ctx exceeded')), True)
test_eq(is_ctx_error(_Fake(), ValueError('KV cache is full')), True)   # matched case-insensitively
test_eq(is_ctx_error(_Fake(), ValueError('connection reset')), False)
```

``` python
class _Full: ctx_limit, pct_full = 8192, 1.0
test_eq(is_ctx_error(_Full(), ValueError('something else')), True)
class _Broken:
    ctx_limit = 8192
    @property
    def pct_full(self): raise RuntimeError('no idea')
test_eq(is_ctx_error(_Broken(), ValueError('unclear')), False)
```

## Finding a backend

`get_runtime(nm)` returns the
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) subclass for
the registered runtime `nm`. It imports the module of the subclass on
the first call. When the import fails, the result depends on the
`optional` field of the
[`Runtime`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#runtime).

``` python
):
```

``` python
register_runtime(Runtime('missing', 'no_such_module_at_all.X', optional=True))
test_fail(lambda: get_runtime('missing'), contains='Install it with')
register_runtime(Runtime('required', 'no_such_module_at_all.X'))
test_fail(lambda: get_runtime('required'), contains='no_such_module_at_all')
del RUNTIMES['missing'], RUNTIMES['required']
```

## The chat

`Chat(model)` returns an instance of the subclass for the runtime of
`model`. A backend writes this subclass. The table shows what a subclass
sets.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Member</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>_runtime</code></td>
<td>The name under which the subclass is registered</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>_opt_map</code>, <code>_opt_skip</code></td>
<td>The option translations described on the <a
href="opts.html">opts</a> page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>_send</code></td>
<td>A method that sends one message and returns the reply</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>_stream</code></td>
<td>A method that does the same and yields chunks</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>_media_ok</code></td>
<td><code>False</code> for a backend that cannot send images or audio.
The default is <code>True</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>_media_note</code></td>
<td>The message of the <code>TypeError</code> that <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat"><code>Chat</code></a>
raises when a message holds media and <code>_media_ok</code> is
<code>False</code>. It says what to use instead</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`media_in` is `True` when pictures that tools return reach the model.
Its default is the value of `_media_ok`. You can set it for a model that
behaves differently.

The settings of a chat are in one
[`ChatOpts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#chatopts)
object, `chat.opts`. `fmt2hist` converts messages in the format of the
backend into the canonical history. `map_opts` translates portable
option names into the names of the backend.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/chat.py#L49"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Chat

``` python
def Chat(
    model:NoneType=None, *, runtime:NoneType=None, model_path:NoneType=None, opts:NoneType=None, **kw
):
```

*A conversation with any registered backend; `Chat(model)` returns the
subclass for the model’s runtime.*

Eight
[`ChatOpts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#chatopts)
fields are also attributes of the chat: `sp`, `approve`, `max_steps`,
`tool_max_len`, `parallel_tools`, `max_parallel_tools`, `final_prompt`
and `ctx`. Each attribute reads `chat.opts`. Setting an attribute
replaces `chat.opts` with a copy that has the new value. The chat keeps
no second copy of the setting.

## Callbacks

`add_cb` attaches a callback to the chat and returns it. You can pass a
callback class, which is instantiated for you, or an instance. `add_cbs`
attaches several. `remove_cb` takes an instance, or a class to remove
every callback of that class, and `remove_cbs` removes several. A
backend’s own default callbacks are attached when the chat is built
unless you pass `default_cbs=False`.

## One turn

`chat(msg)` runs one turn and returns the reply. The `stream` argument
changes the return value.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>stream</code></th>
<th>Return value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>False</code> (default)</td>
<td>The reply</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>True</code></td>
<td>A generator of markdown strings</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>'raw'</code></td>
<td>A generator of the chunk dicts that the backend produced</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The `cbs` argument attaches callbacks for this turn only. Keyword
options such as `temp=0.9` or `effort='high'` also apply to this turn
only. They do not change `chat.opts`. Only the fields in `GEN_OPTS` and
the `extra` options pass through, as
[`turn_kw`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/opts.html#turn_kw)
describes.

When the tool-call budget ends a turn, the chat sends `final_prompt`
once. This asks the model to answer with what it has. A
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) keeps state
between calls. Do not run two turns on one instance at the same time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/chat.py#L150"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Chat.\_\_call\_\_

``` python
def __call__(
    msg:NoneType=None, stream:bool=False, cbs:NoneType=None, **kw
):
```

*Run one chat turn and return the reply.*

`stream=True` returns a generator of markdown. `stream='raw'` returns a
generator of chunk dicts. Keyword options apply only to this turn. A
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) instance is
mutable. It is not safe to run two turns on one instance at the same
time.

### A backend to test against

The examples on this page use `_DemoChat`, a backend that needs no
model. `_DemoChat` appends one `(msg, kw)` pair to `chat.sent` for each
request, where `msg` is the message and `kw` holds the options of that
request. It replies with `echo:` followed by the message text. It is
registered as the `demo` runtime for names that contain `demo-`. It is
also the default runtime. It maps the option `ctx` to `n_ctx` and skips
`effort`.

``` python
class _DemoChat(Chat):
    "A backend that answers without a model, so the machinery around one can be tested."
    _runtime, _opt_map, _opt_skip = 'demo', {'ctx': 'n_ctx'}, ('effort',)
    ctx_limit, token_count = 8192, 0

    def __init__(self, model=None, *, runtime=None, model_path=None, opts=None, **kw):
        self.model_id, self.sent = model, []
        self._setup(model, ChatOpts.create(opts, **kw))

    def _send(self, msg, **kw):
        self.sent.append((msg, kw))
        self.turn_msg = self.mk_msg(msg) if msg is not None else None
        if self.turn_msg: self.hist.append(self.turn_msg)
        self.turn_res = Resp({'role': 'assistant',
                              'content': f'echo: {resp_text(self.turn_msg or {})}'})
        self.hist.append(dict(self.turn_res))
        for _ in run_cbs(self, 'after_response'): pass
        return self.turn_res

    def _stream(self, msg, cbs=None, **kw):
        r = self._send(msg, **kw)
        yield resp_text(r)
        return r

register_runtime(Runtime('demo', _DemoChat, ('demo-',)), dflt=True)
```

``` python
c = Chat('demo-1', sp='Be brief.', ctx=4096, temp=0.2)
test_eq(type(c).__name__, '_DemoChat')           # dispatched by the id pattern
test_eq(isinstance(c, Chat), True)
test_eq((c.sp, c.ctx, c.runtime), ('Be brief.', 4096, 'demo'))
test_eq(c.opts.temp, 0.2)
```

``` python
c.sp = 'Be terse.'
test_eq((c.sp, c.opts.sp), ('Be terse.', 'Be terse.'))
test_fail(lambda: Chat('demo-1', max_parallel_tools=-1), contains='at least 1')
```

``` python
test_eq(c.media_in, True)
c.media_in = False; test_eq(c.media_in, False)
c.media_in = None; test_eq(c.media_in, c._media_ok)
```

``` python
r = c('hello')
test_eq(resp_text(r), 'echo: hello')
test_eq([m['role'] for m in c.hist], ['user', 'assistant'])
test_eq(''.join(c('again', stream=True)), 'echo: again')
```

``` python
c('hi', temp=0.9, effort='high')
test_eq(c.sent[-1][1], {'temp': 0.9, 'effort': 'high'})
test_eq(c.opts.temp, 0.2)
test_eq(c.map_opts({'ctx': 8192, 'effort': 'high'}), {'n_ctx': 8192})
```

``` python
class _Counter(ChatCallback):
    def __init__(self): self.n = 0
    def after_response(self): self.n += 1

c = Chat('demo-1')
cb = c.add_cb(_Counter)
test_eq((isinstance(cb, _Counter), cb.chat is c), (True, True))
c('one'); c('two')
test_eq(cb.n, 2)
```

``` python
c.remove_cb(_Counter)
test_eq(len(c.cbs), 0)
c('three')
test_eq(cb.n, 2)
```

``` python
one_off = _Counter()
c('four', cbs=[one_off])
test_eq((one_off.n, len(c.cbs)), (1, 0))
c('five')
test_eq(one_off.n, 1)
```

## Reconfiguring

Some backends hold state that comes from the system prompt and the
tools. LiteRT keeps a conversation object. MLX keeps a KV cache. If you
assign `chat.sp` directly, that state is out of date.

`reconfigure(sp, tools)` changes the system prompt, the tools, or both.
It keeps the history. It calls the backend hooks so that the backend
rebuilds its state.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Argument value</th>
<th>Effect</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>None</code> (default)</td>
<td>The setting stays as it is</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tools=()</code></td>
<td>Every tool is removed</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A backend implements the hooks `_set_sp`, `_set_tools` and
`_recreate_conv`. The versions in
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) do nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/chat.py#L206"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Chat.reconfigure

``` python
def reconfigure(
    sp:NoneType=None, tools:NoneType=None
):
```

*Change the system prompt or the tools and keep the history; `None`
keeps a value and `tools=()` removes all tools.*

``` python
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    "Add two numbers."
    return a + b

c = Chat('demo-1', sp='old')
c('remember this')
c.reconfigure(sp='new', tools=[add])
test_eq((c.sp, c.opts.sp), ('new', 'new'))
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in c.tools], ['add'])
test_eq(len(c.hist), 2)
```

``` python
c.reconfigure(tools=())
test_eq(list(c.tools), [])
c.reconfigure(sp='newer')
test_eq((list(c.tools), c.sp), ([], 'newer'))
```

## Stopping, and the rest

`cancel()` asks the running turn to stop. You can call it from another
thread, such as the stop button of a user interface. The turn checks the
cancel flag between streamed chunks and between tool calls. It stops at
the next check. Every tool call in the history then has a result, and
the next turn can start normally. A backend that cannot interrupt its
engine finishes the completion that it is generating before it stops.
`cancelled` is `True` while the flag is set. The next turn clears the
flag.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Method</th>
<th>What it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>oneshot(prompt, sp)</code></td>
<td>Asks the model one question outside the conversation, with no tools
and no history, and returns the reply text. <code>hist</code> does not
change</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>recover_context(error)</code></td>
<td>Recovers from a full context window. The version in <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat"><code>Chat</code></a>
raises <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#contextwindowexceedederror"><code>ContextWindowExceededError</code></a>.
A backend that can recover overrides it</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>close()</code></td>
<td>Releases what the backend holds, such as a loaded model</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>print_hist()</code></td>
<td>Shows the whole conversation as markdown</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## Async

[`AsyncChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#asyncchat)
lets async code use any backend. It wraps a
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat), or builds a
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) from the
arguments that you pass. It runs each blocking call in a worker thread,
so the event loop keeps running.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Call</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>await achat(msg)</code></td>
<td>The reply</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>await achat(msg, stream=True)</code></td>
<td>An async iterator of chunks</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

An async generator cannot return a value. The final reply is the
`.value` of the iterator, after you read every chunk.
[`AsyncChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#asyncchat)
reads an attribute that it does not define from the wrapped chat.
`async with` calls `close()` at the end.
[`adisplay_stream`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#adisplay_stream)
is the async version of
[`display_stream`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#display_stream).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/chat.py#L291"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### adisplay_stream

``` python
async def adisplay_stream(
    chunks
):
```

*Show an async markdown stream live in a notebook and return the full
markdown.*

### AsyncChat

``` python
def AsyncChat(
    model:NoneType=None, *, runtime:NoneType=None, **kw
):
```

*An async wrapper around a
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) that runs
its blocking calls in a worker thread.*

``` python
a = AsyncChat('demo-1', sp='async')
test_eq(a.sp, 'async')
test_eq(resp_text(await a('hello')), 'echo: hello')
```

``` python
it = await a('streamed', stream=True)
test_eq([c async for c in it], ['echo: streamed'])
test_eq(resp_text(it.value), 'echo: streamed')
_ = [c async for c in await a('raw', stream='raw')]
test_eq(a.chat._stream_raw, True)    # `stream='raw'` reaches the chat unchanged
```

``` python
async with AsyncChat(Chat('demo-1')) as a2:         # an existing Chat is wrapped, not rebuilt
    test_eq(resp_text(await a2('wrapped')), 'echo: wrapped')
```

## Approving a tool call

The `approve` setting of a chat is a function that takes a tool call. It
returns `True` to run the call and `False` to refuse it. A refused call
gets the result `Denied by human operator`, unless the return value has
a `reply()` method that gives another text. With no `approve` function,
every call runs.

`hitl_policy(modes, ask)` builds an `approve` function from a dict that
maps tool names to modes. HITL means human in the loop.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Mode of the tool</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>approved</code></td>
<td>The call runs. Nobody is asked</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>dont_run</code></td>
<td>The call is refused. Nobody is asked</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Any other mode, or no entry</td>
<td>The function <code>ask</code> decides</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The default `ask` is
[`ask_console`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#ask_console).
It prints the call and waits for `y` or `N`. With `http=True`,
[`hitl_policy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#hitl_policy)
uses
[`http_approval`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#http_approval)
and ignores `ask`.
[`http_approval`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#http_approval)
posts the call to the path `/agent/approval/request` at the address in
the environment variable `URAI_APPROVAL_URL`. The default address is
`http://127.0.0.1:5001`. It raises `RuntimeError` when the request
fails. Pass a URL string as `http` to use another address. The `timeout`
of
[`http_approval`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#http_approval)
is 300 seconds by default.

### ask_console

``` python
def ask_console(
    tc
):
```

*Ask on the console whether tool call `tc` may run.*

``` python
asked = []
p = hitl_policy({'ls': 'approved', 'rm': 'dont_run'}, ask=lambda tc: asked.append(tc) or True)
test_eq(p(ToolCall('ls')), True)
test_eq(p(ToolCall('rm')), False)
test_eq(asked, [])
```

``` python
test_eq(p(ToolCall('anything_else')), True)
test_eq([t.name for t in asked], ['anything_else'])
test_eq(hitl_policy(None, ask=lambda tc: False)(ToolCall('x')), False)
```

``` python
test_fail(lambda: http_approval('http://127.0.0.1:9')(ToolCall('x')),
          contains='approval request failed')
```
